info.title: Portitor connector
info.description: HTTP interface of portitor-connector. The DSP endpoints follow the DSP 2025-1 HTTPS bindings; the message schemas are the official DSP 2025-1 JSON Schemas (copied unchanged in crates/portitor-dsp/tests/schemas). DSP itself publishes no OpenAPI file; this one is written by hand and a test checks that every path in it is served. As consumer, the connector sends callbackAddress = public URL + /dsp/2025-1/callback, so providers call the callback paths below. Every DSP endpoint except /.well-known/dspace-version needs a DCP self-issued ID token (ADR 0016), and the caller's credential service must present a valid MembershipCredential from a trusted issuer, in presentations whose every credential passes its checks (DCP v1.0.1, 5.4.3; since 1.1 a valid token alone is enough to end one's own transfer, TD-47); otherwise the answer is the endpoint's DSP error with reason "unauthorized": with HTTP 404 on the negotiation and transfer endpoints, callbacks included (DSP 2025-1 HTTPS bindings, "Unauthorized Access": a client that is not authorized gets 404; Eclipse EDC answers the same), and with HTTP 401 on the catalog endpoints (ADR 0016, amended in 0.12). The reason is in the connector's log. When the caller could not be checked because a service the check needs did not answer, the answer is 503 with a problem document, so that a partner tries again. /health and the data plane (/data, its own tokens) are open. Known limits (docs/RISKS_AND_TECHNICAL_DEBTS.md): a negotiation starts from the consumer only, so the DSP consumer endpoint POST /dsp/2025-1/callback/negotiations/offers, with which a provider starts one, is not served (TD-35); Policies are read strictly (ADR 0009, amended 2026-11-18): an offer or agreement with a field this connector does not know is refused with 400, and the reason names the field. Three answers are the same on every route and are a problem document (application/problem+json), not a DSP error, because they are made outside the handlers: 413 when the request body is over the route's limit, 503 when the request took longer than 60 seconds, and 500 when a handler hit a bug (a panic; the server goes on, the error is logged and counted in portitor.http.request.panicked).

400.description: Invalid message

401.description: The caller is not authenticated (DCP); the body is the endpoint's DSP error with code "401" and reason "unauthorized"

post.description: The whole catalog comes in one answer: there are no pages and no Link header. A filter that is empty, or an EDC QuerySpec with only paging and sorting (offset, limit, sortOrder, sortField), gets the whole catalog; paging and sorting are ignored. Any other filter is refused with 400 (TD-36).

post.description: The consumer sends a request for an offer from the catalog. The provider answers with its acknowledgement, then sends its next message (offer, agreement or termination) to the consumer's callbackAddress. An offer with credential constraints (ADR 0019) is agreed only if the consumer's credential service presents the credentials they name with matching claims; the provider asks it for their scopes with the access token the consumer sent.

post.description: Accepted from the counter-party in every state that is not final (DSP 2025-1: the message "MAY be sent at any state"; the state machine figure is narrower; ADR 0006, amended 2026-11-18).

The consumer asks for a dataset under a finalized agreement it holds, in a format the dataset offers (ADR 0013): pull (HttpData-PULL) or, since 1.1, push (HttpData-PUSH, ADR 0027), where the request carries the consumer's dataAddress (endpointType https://w3id.org/dspace-sig/profile/http-push) and the provider's data plane sends the data to it once the transfer is STARTED. The provider answers with its acknowledgement, then sends a TransferStartMessage with the data address (or a termination) to the consumer's callbackAddress. An agreement with credential constraints (ADR 0019) is checked again with fresh credentials, so a revoked credential ends the transfer. A request that the same consumer sends again with the same consumerPid starts nothing new: the answer is the transfer it already has, in its current state, and no second data address or token is sent (DSP 2025-1, Transfer Request Message: idempotent behavior based on consumerPid; ADR 0013, amended in 0.12). If its agreementId, format or callbackAddress differ from the first request, it is refused with 400.

201.description: Transfer created (state REQUESTED); or, for a repeated request, the transfer that already exists, in its current state

400.description: Invalid message, no finalized agreement for the caller, format not offered or not supported, a dataAddress in a pull request, a push request whose dataAddress is missing, not https:// (unless PORTITOR_ALLOW_HTTP) or not of the push profile, or refused callback address, or a consumerPid the caller already used for another transfer request

get.summary: The data of a started transfer
get.description: Open route with its own token: the bearer token from the transfer's data address (DSP dataAddress, endpointProperties "authorization"). Valid while the transfer is STARTED and for PORTITOR_DATA_TOKEN_SECONDS after the start. Streams the source's 2xx answer with its Content-Type; the source URL is never shown. Since 1.1 (ADR 0027): the source may also be an object of the provider's object storage (s3://{bucket}/{key}); the consumer's MembershipCredential, kept from its transfer request, is checked again on each request and while the data streams. A membership that no longer holds gets 401 and ends the transfer; a running download is cut (the connection ends before the data does) when the membership fails or the transfer is suspended or terminated.

200.description: The data, streamed from the dataset's source

401.description: No token, a wrong or expired token, or an unknown flow; since 1.1 also a consumer whose membership no longer holds or could not be checked now

500.description: The store could not be read (no body), or a bug in the handler (a problem document)

502.description: The source did not answer with 2xx; for an s3:// source, also a connector without object storage

post.summary: Receive the data of a push transfer (since 1.1)
post.description: Open route with its own token, on a connector with object storage settings and PORTITOR_PUSH_BUCKET (ADR 0027): the provider's data plane sends the data of a push transfer (format HttpData-PUSH) this connector asked for. The endpoint and the bearer token are those of the dataAddress in our transfer request (endpointType https://w3id.org/dspace-sig/profile/http-push). The token is valid while the transfer is REQUESTED or STARTED and for PORTITOR_DATA_TOKEN_SECONDS after the request (or the last start again). The body is streamed into the push bucket as the object named {consumerPid}, with its Content-Type; a second request replaces the object. POST and PUT do the same: the HTTP Transfer Profile names no method. Not subject to PORTITOR_MAX_REQUEST_BYTES nor to the request time limit.

204.description: The data is in the push bucket

400.description: The request body broke off; nothing was stored

401.description: No token, a wrong or expired token, an unknown transfer, or a transfer that is not REQUESTED or STARTED

500.description: The store could not be read or written (no body), or a bug in the handler (a problem document)

502.description: The object storage refused the data or did not answer; nothing was stored

put.summary: Receive the data of a push transfer (since 1.1)
put.description: Open route with its own token, on a connector with object storage settings and PORTITOR_PUSH_BUCKET (ADR 0027): the provider's data plane sends the data of a push transfer (format HttpData-PUSH) this connector asked for. The endpoint and the bearer token are those of the dataAddress in our transfer request (endpointType https://w3id.org/dspace-sig/profile/http-push). The token is valid while the transfer is REQUESTED or STARTED and for PORTITOR_DATA_TOKEN_SECONDS after the request (or the last start again). The body is streamed into the push bucket as the object named {consumerPid}, with its Content-Type; a second request replaces the object. POST and PUT do the same: the HTTP Transfer Profile names no method. Not subject to PORTITOR_MAX_REQUEST_BYTES nor to the request time limit.

204.description: The data is in the push bucket

400.description: The request body broke off; nothing was stored

401.description: No token, a wrong or expired token, an unknown transfer, or a transfer that is not REQUESTED or STARTED

500.description: The store could not be read or written (no body), or a bug in the handler (a problem document)

502.description: The object storage refused the data or did not answer; nothing was stored

dcp.description: DCP 1.0 self-issued ID token, signed by the caller's DID key, carrying an access token for its credential service in the token claim

Problem.description: An error, as RFC 9457 problem details.

title.description: Short summary of the problem type.

detail.description: What went wrong in this case.

PayloadTooLarge.description: The request body is over the route's limit: 64 KiB on the routes whose messages are small by specification (catalog request; negotiation event, verification and termination; transfer suspension, completion and termination), PORTITOR_MAX_REQUEST_BYTES (default 2 MiB) on the others

InternalError.description: A bug in the handler (a panic): the error is logged and counted (portitor.http.request.panicked), and the server goes on

Unavailable.description: The caller could not be checked now, because a service the check needs (a DID document, a credential service, a status list, this connector's own STS) did not answer; or the request took longer than 60 seconds. Try again later

TransferBusy.description: As Unavailable (a problem document: the caller could not be checked now, or the request took longer than 60 seconds); or, from 1.2, another call is changing the transfer now: it holds the transfer's lease in the database while its data plane step runs (TD-48). Nothing was written; the answer is the endpoint's DSP error with code "503" and reason "the transfer is being changed; retry", with Retry-After: 1. DSP 2025-1 says only that a refused message answers 4xx; Eclipse EDC answers a process it is changing with 503 too, because its consumers retry a 5xx and end the transfer on a 4xx (ADR 0007, note added in 1.2). Try again later

Retry-After.description: Seconds to wait before trying again: 1, for a transfer that is being changed

TookTooLong.description: The request took longer than 60 seconds, or waited that long for a free slot (256 requests are worked on at once)
